related_questions.question: What triggers Sjögren's flare?
related_questions.snippet: In Sjögren's syndrome, the immune system attacks the tear and saliva glands, and other secretory glands throughout the body. The reasons for this remains unknown, but research suggests that it's triggered by a combination of genetic, environmental and, possibly, hormonal factors.

related_questions.question: How do you treat Sjogren's symptoms?

text_blocks.snippet: Sjögren's syndrome primarily affects the eyes and mouth, causing dryness. While there's no cure, treatment focuses on symptom management and preventing complications. This includes artificial tears and saliva substitutes, medications to stimulate saliva production, and addressing other symptoms like joint pain with NSAIDs or corticosteroids.
snippet_highlighted_words: artificial tears and saliva substitutes, medications to stimulate saliva production, and addressing other symptoms like joint pain with NSAIDs or corticosteroids

list.title: Dry Eyes:
list.snippet: Artificial tears, eye gels, and prescription eye drops like cyclosporine (Restasis) or lifitegrast (Xiidra) can help relieve dryness. Moisture chamber spectacles and plugs in the tear ducts can also be beneficial.

list.title: Dry Mouth:
list.snippet: Drinking water, chewing sugar-free gum, and using saliva substitutes can help. Prescription medications like pilocarpine (Salagen) or cevimeline (Evoxac) can stimulate saliva production.

list.title: Joint Pain:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter NSAIDs (like ibuprofen) can help manage mild pain. For more severe pain, corticosteroids or disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs (DMARDs) like hydroxychloroquine or methotrexate may be prescribed.

list.title: Other Symptoms:
list.snippet: Depending on the specific symptoms and organ involvement, doctors may prescribe medications to address fatigue, skin dryness, vaginal dryness, or other systemic issues.

list.title: Regular Checkups:
list.snippet: Regular monitoring by a rheumatologist is crucial to assess disease progression and manage potential complications.

list.title: Lifestyle Modifications:
list.snippet: Staying hydrated, using a humidifier, avoiding smoking and dry environments, and practicing good oral hygiene can help manage symptoms.

list.title: Medication Management:
list.snippet: It's important to inform your doctor about all medications you're taking, as some can worsen dryness.

list.title: New Treatments:
list.snippet: Research continues to explore new treatment options, including medications like dazodalibep, ianalumab, and nipocalimab, which are in clinical trials.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, treatment for Sjögren's syndrome is tailored to the individual's specific symptoms and involves a combination of symptom management strategies, medications, and lifestyle adjustments.

related_questions.question: What is the life expectancy of someone with Sjogren's syndrome?

text_blocks.snippet: Most people with Sjögren's syndrome, particularly those with primary Sjögren's and only mild symptoms, have a life expectancy comparable to the general population. However, the disease's impact on quality of life can be significant due to symptoms like dry eyes and mouth, fatigue, and pain. In some cases, Sjögren's can lead to serious complications, such as lymphoma or lung disease, which may affect life expectancy.
snippet_highlighted_words: Most people with Sjögren's syndrome, particularly those with primary Sjögren's and only mild symptoms, have a life expectancy comparable to the general population

list.title: Primary vs. Secondary Sjögren's:
list.snippet: Primary Sjögren's syndrome (pSS) is diagnosed when the condition is the main illness. Secondary Sjögren's occurs when it's associated with another autoimmune disease. While pSS generally has a good prognosis, secondary Sjögren's life expectancy is more tied to the primary disease.

list.title: Disease Severity and Complications:
list.snippet: Individuals with more severe forms of Sjögren's, particularly those experiencing complications like lung disease (ILD) or lymphoma, may have a reduced life expectancy.

list.title: Early Diagnosis and Management:
list.snippet: Early diagnosis and effective management of Sjögren's syndrome, including addressing systemic manifestations and complications, can significantly improve a patient's quality of life and potentially extend their lifespan.

list.title: Comorbidities:
list.snippet: Conditions like cardiovascular disease and infections, which can be more prevalent or severe in individuals with Sjögren's, may also impact life expectancy.

list.title: Individual Factors:
list.snippet: Age at diagnosis, sex, and the presence of other health conditions can influence the course and prognosis of Sjögren's.

text_blocks.snippet: Overall, while Sjögren's syndrome can present challenges and impact quality of life, most individuals with the condition can expect to live a normal lifespan with proper management and monitoring, according to the Cleveland Clinic and the Sjögren's Foundation.

text_blocks.snippet: Surgeons disease, also known as Sjögren's syndrome, is a chronic autoimmune disease characterized by dry eyes and dry mouth, but it can also affect other parts of the body. Symptoms vary greatly, with some individuals experiencing mild discomfort while others have debilitating symptoms that impact their quality of life.

list.snippet: Dry Eyes: Burning, itching, gritty sensation, blurred vision, and sensitivity to light.
Dry Mouth: Difficulty chewing, swallowing, speaking, and a dry, sore throat.
Fatigue: Significant tiredness and exhaustion.
Joint Pain: Pain, stiffness, and swelling, often in the hands, feet, and knees.
Swollen Salivary Glands: Especially around the jaw and ears.
Skin Issues: Dryness, rashes, or Raynaud's phenomenon (cold hands and feet).
Other Symptoms: Vaginal dryness, cough, shortness of breath, gastrointestinal problems, and neurological issues can also occur.

text_blocks.snippet: While dry eyes and mouth are the most prominent, Sjögren's can affect other organs, including:

list.snippet: Lungs: Cough, shortness of breath, and potentially interstitial lung disease.
Kidneys: Abnormal kidney function.
Nervous System: Neuropathy (numbness, pain, tingling), "brain fog", and in rare cases, inflammation of the brain.
Gastrointestinal Tract: Heartburn, reflux, and other digestive issues.
Blood Vessels: Raynaud's phenomenon.
Liver: Abnormal liver function.
Many conditions can cause dry eyes and mouth, so it's crucial to see a healthcare professional for proper diagnosis.
Symptoms can be mild to severe and may fluctuate over time.
Some symptoms, like dry eyes and mouth, can increase the risk of infections.
Sjögren's can increase the risk of lymphoma.
